must_find.summary: v-if and v-for are on the same <li>. In Vue 3, v-if has higher priority than v-for, so `event` is undefined when the v-if is evaluated: the template errors and the Hide logins filter doesn't work. Move the login filter into the computed (or a <template v-for> wrapper).

50k never-edited events are stored in a deep ref, so Vue wraps every object in a reactive proxy (slow, memory-heavy) and every access is tracked. Use shallowRef (or markRaw) for requirement 1/2's read-only data.
watch(events, ..., { deep: true }) traverses all 50k objects on every change (including the sort's in-place reordering), and the deletes count belongs in a computed anyway.

The matching computed calls events.value.sort(...), mutating its own reactive source inside a computed (a side effect that re-triggers dependents and the deep watcher), and re-sorts 50k items on every keystroke. Sort once on load (or copy), and only filter in the computed.

window resize listener is added in onMounted and never removed (no onUnmounted / onBeforeUnmount), and it keeps the component instance alive. Since the feed mounts and unmounts repeatedly, listeners and components leak (requirement 5).

nice_to_find.summary: All matching rows (up to 50k <li>) are rendered; vue-virtual-scroller is available but unused (requirement 2).
The 'N events' count uses matching.length, which doesn't apply the Hide logins toggle.
fetchEvents errors aren't handled in onMounted.

must_not_flag.summary: v-memo keyed on [event.id, selected] is a valid optimization for these immutable rows; NOT a stale-render bug.
v-once on the static toolbar is harmless. Calling it redundant (Vue already hoists static content) is a fair Suggestion and does NOT count as flagged; only presenting it as a bug counts.
Creating the Intl.DateTimeFormat once in setup (not per row) is correct.
